o1.biggest_strength: It targets the real leak, Essentials 8+ churn, with a clear flat Agency plan, honest customer messaging, and a test that measures both uptake and Team cannibalization.
o1.biggest_mistake: It only lightly uses the under-used yearly billing lever, even though the data shows a large churn gap and this is a cheap near-term win.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a clearer yearly-billing push for all eligible customers after signup and tighten the month-6 revenue table so each churn and revenue assumption is fully traceable.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a strong Agency-plan shape with a useful one-user guardrail, transparent pricing-page copy, and a smart pre-check for Team downgrade risk.
o2.biggest_mistake: It dismisses yearly billing as a runner-up despite the data showing yearly payers churn far less, and its first live test focuses on new visitors rather than the existing at-risk cohort driving the leak.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Test the Agency plan directly with existing Essentials 8+ customers while adding an honest in-app yearly offer, and clean up the few inconsistent revenue assumptions.

reason: Output 1 is more directly usable because it acts on the main churn pool immediately and gives a practical existing-customer test with stop rules. Output 2 has good ideas, but it underplays the yearly-billing signal and tests away from the biggest revenue leak first.
